stage1.impression: A clean, well-composed three-quarter studio shot of a tinted-acrylic turntable with a believable tonearm and a soft key. It is spoiled by the plinth's front and side edges, which render as near-black slabs broken by rectangular, posterised patches of saturated royal blue, a refraction or denoiser artefact that no real acrylic produces. Together with the CG-clean floor and the glassy, shadowless lower deck, it reads as a good render, not a photograph.

reads_as: a Pro-Ject/Clearaudio-style clear acrylic deck on a floating sub-plinth

unreal.what: The edges of the top plinth render near-black (lum about 44, neutral grey) with blocky, hard-edged rectangles of saturated royal blue (RGB about 41/54/114) scattered along them, like posterised or denoised caustics. The pale Ice tint never shows on the edge.
unreal.real: A polished edge on pale through-tinted cast acrylic glows: it gathers light internally and shows a brighter, more saturated cyan-ice band, with smooth reflections of the softbox and room. No rectangles, and never darker than the face. Fix the IOR/thickness or volume absorption so the edge carries the tint, add more transmission/volume bounces and samples, and drop or soften the denoiser on glass.

unreal.what: The sub-plinth reads as a smoked mirror with a hard black inner rectangle drawn around it, darker and greyer than the Ice top, as if it were a different material. It casts almost no shadow onto the floor.
unreal.real: A second sheet of the same Ice acrylic would show the same pale tint, a softer polished edge glow and a coloured transmitted shadow and caustic on the floor. A rebate or chamfer would read as a thin bright line, not a black outline.

unreal.what: The isolation feet or couplers between the decks are a muddy jumble of refracted fragments with black specks. They do not read as machined parts.
unreal.real: Machined aluminium or steel cones or sorbothane pucks with a crisp turned profile, a clean chamfer and a visible contact point, seen undistorted through polished acrylic.

unreal.what: The floor contact is weak. The product floats with only a faint blurred shadow under the feet, and there is no contact shadow line along the sub-plinth.
unreal.real: A tight, dark contact occlusion under each foot, a soft, broad shadow under the whole footprint and a blue-tinted transmitted light pool from the acrylic on the white sweep.

unreal.what: The EARF wordmark is a flat white decal sitting on a blue rectangle. It looks pasted on, with no depth, engraving or print layer.
unreal.real: A laser-engraved or reverse-printed mark inside the edge: a frosted engraving that catches light or a crisp pad print with a tiny parallax, scaled to about 6-8 mm cap height.

unreal.what: The platter rim reads as stacked blue and white plastic rings with an unexplained white band and a deep saturated blue that does not match the Ice plinth.
unreal.real: A single thick acrylic or aluminium platter with a polished or bead-blasted rim, one consistent material and a visible belt groove or subplatter.

unreal.what: The headshell and cartridge are thin, generic flat plates with oversized round screws. There is no stylus or cantilever, and the tag clamp reads as a stamped part.
unreal.real: A die-cast headshell with a finger lift, a real cartridge body with its stylus guard off, a visible cantilever and two slotted M2.5 screws with nuts.

unreal.what: The armrest post is a plain tube with no lift or cue lever. The arm sits away from it, and the cue is missing.
unreal.real: An arm lift tower with a damped cue lever and a cradle the arm actually rests in, or the arm parked on it in a hero shot.

unreal.what: The background is a dark grey band (lum about 62) meeting a white sweep with a hard, diagonal falloff, so the set looks like a CG ground plane at a horizon.
unreal.real: A continuous paper or plaster cove that grades smoothly from lit floor to a softly darker back wall, with no visible edge.

unreal.what: The motor pod or puck at the back-left corner is a featureless chrome disc. It is unclear what it is, and the 'ST...TA' label text is faint and illegible.
unreal.real: A defined motor pod with a turned pulley and a visible belt. A record label with legible printed type at proper contrast.

cooler.idea: Make the tint the hero. Let the thick plinth edges glow pale ice-blue as light-piping slabs, maybe with a frosted underside, so the colour reads as a material that only cast acrylic can do.
cooler.now: A generic clear-acrylic deck (Pro-Ject Acryl, Clearaudio Emotion) with dark edges.

cooler.idea: Give the two-deck stack a deliberate, visible decoupling detail: large machined bronze or steel pucks set into counterbores, read as jewellery between the sheets.
cooler.now: Anonymous feet hidden in refraction, like a lab rig.

cooler.idea: Draw a signature tonearm, such as a tapered, polished or tinted-acrylic armtube with a sculpted counterweight, instead of the stock straight tube and pillar.
cooler.now: A Rega RB-style arm on a generic base, so the deck borrows its identity.

cooler.idea: Integrate the motor and the controls into the plinth form, for example a recessed motor in a cast pocket with a single knurled speed dial, so the top surface has one composed gesture.
cooler.now: Parts scattered on a flat slab, the usual acrylic-turntable kit look.

cooler.idea: Shape the plinth in plan, with radiused corners or a cut that echoes the platter, so its silhouette is recognisable without the logo.
cooler.now: A plain rectangle with sharp-ish corners, the default archetype.

photo.change: Fix the acrylic: a correct IOR (1.49), volume absorption in the Ice tint, raised glossy/transmission/volume bounces (12+), more samples and no aggressive denoise on glass.
photo.expected: The edges glow pale blue without blocky patches. This alone removes the main CG tell (+1.5).

photo.change: Add a long rim/strip light behind and to the left, plus a white card in front low, to send light into the edges and to draw clean highlight lines on the top and edge chamfers.
photo.expected: Crisp outlines on the two sheets and luminous edges, so it reads as a studio photograph.

photo.change: Replace the horizon with a seamless curved cove and a gentle gradient, and add contact occlusion and caustics under the feet.
photo.expected: The product sits on the set rather than floating in front of a CG plane.

photo.change: Lower the camera slightly and use a longer lens (about 85-100 mm equivalent) with shallow focus falling off at the back corner.
photo.expected: Less wide-angle distortion, more premium compression and a real-lens feel.

photo.change: Add surface realism: faint micro-scratches and dust on the acrylic top, a slight anisotropy on the turned metal, and a legible printed label on the record.
photo.expected: Breaks up the CG-clean surfaces and gives real scale cues.
